This was required because LocalizationService is a singleton and parallel test class execution caused concurrent SetCulture calls to corrupt state — IClassFixture alone was insufficient.

comments.note: LocaleSequentialCollection.cs was added beyond the WP spec to address a parallel-execution hazard: LocalizationService is a singleton, and IClassFixture<T> alone does not prevent concurrent culture changes from other test classes running in parallel. The [CollectionDefinition(DisableParallelization=true)] with ICollectionFixture<EnglishLocaleFixture> ensures all 5 locale-sensitive classes run sequentially with a single shared fixture. This is the correct xUnit pattern for tests that share global mutable state.

comments.note: LocaleSequentialCollection.cs now serves purely as a DisableParallelization=true grouping mechanism. Each of the 5 classes has its own IClassFixture<EnglishLocaleFixture> instance — meaning EnglishLocaleFixture is constructed/disposed once per test class (not once per test). The xUnit fixture lifecycle is: IClassFixture<T> = per-class, ICollectionFixture<T> = per-collection. With DisableParallelization=true on the collection, classes still run sequentially, preventing the LocalizationService singleton race condition. Both invariants are now satisfied: the literal AC requirement (IClassFixture + constructor injection) and the safety requirement (sequential execution).

The `_ = localeFixture;` discard pattern is used in all 5 constructors to acknowledge the fixture parameter without storing it — the fixture's work is done in its own constructor. This pattern is idiomatic for fixtures whose sole purpose is setup/teardown side effects. No separate field reference is needed.

summary: Reviewed all 8 files modified by the WP-001 implementation: EnglishLocaleFixture.cs, LocaleSequentialCollection.cs, the 5 locale-sensitive test classes, and LocalizationServiceTests.cs.

EnglishLocaleFixture.cs: Clean IDisposable implementation. Correctly snapshots CurrentCulture on construction and restores on Dispose(). No unmanaged resources — GC.SuppressFinalize not needed. Single responsibility, correct contract.

LocaleSequentialCollection.cs: Lean and purposeful. The XML doc comment accurately explains the singleton-race rationale. The public const Name avoids magic string duplication across all 5 consuming test classes — good design.

All 5 test classes (GameLauncherCoordinatorTests, StatusCoordinatorTests, UpdateCheckCoordinatorTests, DiffServiceTests, ProfileServiceTests): Consistent IClassFixture<EnglishLocaleFixture> + constructor injection pattern. The _ = localeFixture discard with inline comment is idiomatic and self-documenting. [Collection(LocaleSequentialCollection.Name)] correctly prevents parallel execution to protect the LocalizationService singleton.

LocalizationServiceTests.CurrentCulture_DefaultsToSystemCulture: Well-designed locale-agnostic contract test. Reads SessionStartCulture (immutable snapshot from singleton construction), asserts parseability, then conditionally checks system locale match — does NOT call SetCulture() so singleton state is never mutated by this test. Correct and future-proof.

Fix-Forward applied: IsParseable() bare catch narrowed to catch (CultureNotFoundException). The original bare catch swallowed all exception types including catastrophic exceptions (OutOfMemoryException, etc.). Narrowing to CultureNotFoundException is semantically precise and non-behavioral (CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo throws CultureNotFoundException for invalid culture names).

Overall: Architecture is correct. The dual-mechanism approach — IClassFixture<T> for per-class setup/teardown plus DisableParallelization=true via collection for sequential execution — is the right pattern for tests sharing a global mutable singleton. Clean, maintainable, well-commented.

comments.note: LocalizationServiceTests.IsParseable(): Changed bare `catch` to `catch (CultureNotFoundException)`. The original swallowed all exception types including catastrophic ones (OutOfMemoryException, ThreadAbortException). CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo() throws CultureNotFoundException for invalid culture names — this is the only exception the helper should intercept. Non-behavioral change: the observable test behavior is identical since only CultureNotFoundException occurs in practice.

[documentation-forward] EnglishLocaleFixture.cs has no XML doc comment. Future contributors adding new locale-sensitive test classes need to know: (1) what this fixture does (forces en-US via LocalizationService singleton for the duration of a test class), (2) why it requires IClassFixture<T> pairing with [Collection(LocaleSequentialCollection.Name)] to prevent concurrent culture mutations from parallel test classes, and (3) the expected usage pattern (constructor injection with _ = localeFixture discard). A class-level /// <summary> covering these three points would make the fixture self-discoverable.

DiffServiceTests and ProfileServiceTests are not marked `sealed`, unlike the three coordinator test classes. Pre-existing inconsistency — xUnit test classes typically benefit from `sealed` (prevents accidental subclassing and enables minor JIT optimizations). Not introduced by this WP; worth addressing in a future cleanup pass for consistency.
